nodes.question: What type of information is needed for the environmental mapping and assessment in the Athens Metropolitan Area?
nodes.answer: Up-to-date and reliable information such as geospatial, remote sensing, in situ observational, and numerical modelling data is needed for the environmental mapping and assessment in the Athens Metropolitan Area.
nodes.paragraph: To meet these multifaceted goals, extensive and holistic mapping and assessment of all environmental pressures is needed, based on up-to-date and reliable information such as geospatial, remote sensing, in situ observational and numerical modelling data. Athens Metropolitan Area (AMA), which holds the 14th place in the European ranking for cities regarding population density (https:// ec. europa. eu/ euros tat/) in a country (Greece) where 80.36% (reference year 2022) of the population is liv - ing in urban areas ( https:// datab ank. world bank. org/) faces multiple pressures, among which urban climate variability, urban excess heat, air quality degradation, and lack of green spaces, prevail (Asprogerakas 2016). nodes.question: What remains underexplored regarding GIS and RS according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The inter-relationships and combined impacts of GIS and RS data on UBS, UGS, and chlorophyll are underexplored.
nodes.paragraph: 2021). The advancement of modern technological tools like geographic information systems (GIS) and remote sens- ing (RS) have revolutionized environmental monitoring and management. These tools enable the coverage of large areas and facilitate the acquisition of data from inaccessible locations, surpassing the limitations of traditional studies (Barraza-Moraga et al. 2022; Ouma et al. 2020). They have become essential in monitoring and managing environmen- tal changes effectively, utilizing multi-temporal satellite imagery for quantitative assessments (Barraza-Moraga et al. 2022; Majumder et al. 2023; Rejaur Rahman and Rahman 2023). Remote sensing has been widely applied to identify UBS and UGS spaces, while its potential for monitoring chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) has expanded beyond the constraints of traditional active techniques (Ayeni and Adesalu 2018; Barraza-Moraga et al. 2022; Bramich et al. 2021; Zarco- Tejada et al. 2019).
